slides.title: The Prompt Was Versioned. The Text Kept Changing.
slides.subtitle: An admissions calling platform. Code read at the commit pinned on 19 September 2026, rows read on 28 September 2026.
slides.caption: Every answer this platform's AI writes is stamped with the prompt family, the version and the model that produced it.

slides.title: The stamp is real.
slides.subtitle: Every AI result row carries a family, a version and a model.
slides.caption: Across every stamped row there is one version and one model, and not a single row is missing its stamp.

rows: across every stamped row in the two result tables

distinct models across every stamped row
slides.caption: Read from the platform's own tables on 28 September 2026.
The stamp, on a keyless local copy of the platform at the pinned commit seeded with invented rows. Three prompt families, every one of them at the same version.

slides.title: The version did not move. The text did.
slides.subtitle: Two edits landed on prompt text without the version changing.
slides.caption: A version is a promise that the same text produced the same answers, and two edits to prompt text landed without it changing.

rows: stamped rows produced by prompt text that changed under an unchanged version
registered family and version pairs that appear on any stamped row
registered prompt families that appear on any stamped row
slides.caption: Six families are registered and three of them ever ran, so most of the library is a catalogue of things nothing calls.
The page that reports on the AI's own output names the calls, the intents and the consent split, and never names the prompt behind any of them.
Every setting an operator can change, and none of them is a prompt. The text lives in source files, so changing a word is a deploy.

slides.caption: The voice script is prompt text too, and it carries no version at all.

slides.title: A stamp that cannot tell you which text ran.
slides.subtitle: The version is recorded on every row and displayed on no screen.
slides.caption: The stamp is not the problem. A stamp that cannot tell you which text ran is the problem, and no screen in the product shows it.
